ei.title: Chapter 1-03 2번: Solving the Puzzle of Your Life
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: Just as you don't know everything in advance about a trip you are going to take, neither can you know everything about how your new life or career might unfold. But that's fine. You just have to treat it like doing a jigsaw: accept that the full picture is going to emerge gradually rather than instantly. While sometimes it will be straightforward to fit pieces together, at other times it will take more effort and patience. Sometimes you will find interesting pieces that open up a whole new section, and at other times you may find pieces that don't seem to belong anywhere right now. You just need to keep at it until the picture emerges and you can see clearly what you have achieved.

questions.passage: Just as you don't know everything in advance about a trip you are going to take, neither can you know everything about how your new life or career might (A)[unfold / collapse]. But that's fine. You just have to treat it like doing a jigsaw: accept that the full picture is going to emerge (B)[gradually / suddenly] rather than instantly. While sometimes it will be straightforward to fit pieces together, at other times it will take more effort and (C)[patience / haste]. Sometimes you will find interesting pieces that open up a whole new section, and at other times you may find pieces that don't seem to belong anywhere right now. You just need to keep at it until the picture emerges and you can see clearly what you have achieved.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 새로운 삶이 어떻게 펼쳐질지(unfold), 그림이 점진적으로(gradually) 드러나며, 더 많은 노력과 인내(patience)가 필요하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① collapse — gradually — patience (A 반대: 펼쳐지다→무너지다)
✅ ② unfold — gradually — patience — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ unfold — suddenly — patience (B 반대: 점진적으로→갑자기)
❌ ④ unfold — gradually — haste (C 반대: 인내→성급함)

questions.passage: Just as you don't know everything in advance about a trip you are going to take, neither can you know everything about how your new life or career might unfold. But that's fine. You just have to treat it like doing a jigsaw: accept that the full picture is going to emerge gradually rather than instantly. While sometimes it will be (A)[straightforward / complicated] to fit pieces together, at other times it will take more effort and patience. Sometimes you will find (B)[interesting / boring] pieces that open up a whole new section, and at other times you may find pieces that don't seem to belong anywhere right now. You just need to keep at it until the picture emerges and you can see clearly what you have (C)[achieved / abandoned].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 때로는 조각들을 맞추기가 간단할(straightforward) 것이고, 흥미로운(interesting) 조각들을 발견하며, 무엇을 성취했는지(achieved) 볼 수 있다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① complicated — interesting — achieved (A 반대: 간단한→복잡한)
❌ ② straightforward — boring — achieved (B 반대: 흥미로운→지루한)
✅ ③ straightforward — interesting — achieved — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ straightforward — interesting — abandoned (C 반대: 성취하다→포기하다)

questions.passage: Just as you don't know everything in (A)[advance / retrospect] about a trip you are going to take, neither can you know everything about how your new life or career might unfold. But that's fine. You just have to treat it like doing a jigsaw: accept that the full picture is going to (B)[emerge / vanish] gradually rather than instantly. While sometimes it will be straightforward to fit pieces together, at other times it will take more effort and patience. Sometimes you will find interesting pieces that open up a whole new section, and at other times you may find pieces that don't seem to (C)[belong / dominate] anywhere right now. You just need to keep at it until the picture emerges and you can see clearly what you have achieved.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 여행에 대해 미리(in advance) 모든 것을 알 수 없고, 전체 그림이 드러나며(emerge), 어디에도 속하지(belong) 않는 것처럼 보이는 조각들도 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① advance — emerge — belong — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ② retrospect — emerge — belong (A 반대: 미리→회고하여)
❌ ③ advance — vanish — belong (B 반대: 드러나다→사라지다)
❌ ④ advance — emerge — dominate (C 반대: 속하다→지배하다)
det.tip: in advance(미리) ↔ in retrospect(돌이켜보면), emerge(나타나다) ↔ vanish(사라지다)

questions.passage: Just as you don't know everything in advance about a trip you are going to take, neither can you know everything about how your new life or career might unfold. But that's fine. You just have to ①<u>treat</u> it like doing a jigsaw: ②<u>accept</u> that the full picture is going to emerge ③<u>instantly</u> rather than instantly. While sometimes it will be straightforward to fit pieces together, at other times it will take more ④<u>effort</u> and patience. Sometimes you will find interesting pieces that open up a whole new section, and at other times you may find pieces that don't seem to belong anywhere right now. You just need to keep at it until the picture emerges and you can see clearly what you have achieved.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: '즉시(instantly)'가 아니라 '점진적으로(gradually)'가 문맥상 적절하다. 전체 그림이 즉시가 아닌 점진적으로 드러난다.
det.analysis:
① treat — 다루다, 원문 일치
② accept — 받아들이다, 원문 일치
③ instantly — 원문은 gradually(점진적으로) ←정답
④ effort — 노력, 원문 일치

questions.passage: Just as you don't know everything in ①<u>advance</u> about a trip you are going to take, neither can you know everything about how your new life or career might unfold. While sometimes it will be straightforward to ②<u>scatter</u> pieces together, at other times it will take more effort and patience. Sometimes you will find interesting pieces that open up a whole new ③<u>section</u>, and at other times you may find pieces that don't seem to belong anywhere right now. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: '흩뿌리다(scatter)'가 아니라 '맞추다(fit)'가 문맥상 적절하다. 조각들을 함께 맞추는 것이지 흩뿌리는 것이 아니다.
det.analysis:
① advance — 미리, 원문 일치
② scatter — 원문은 fit(맞추다) ←정답
③ section — 부분, 원문 일치
④ clearly — 분명하게, 원문 일치

questions.passage: Just as you don't know everything in advance about a trip you are going to take, neither can you know everything about how your new life or career might unfold. det.korean: '포기하다(give up on)'가 아니라 '계속하다(keep at)'가 문맥상 적절하다. 그림이 드러날 때까지 계속해야 한다.
det.analysis:
① fine — 괜찮은, 원문 일치
② straightforward — 간단한, 원문 일치
③ interesting — 흥미로운, 원문 일치
④ give up on — 원문은 keep at(계속하다) ←정답
det.tip: keep at(계속하다, 꾸준히 하다) ↔ give up on(포기하다)

❌ ③ take more effort — 더 많은 노력을 들이다 (필요 조건이지 행동 지속 아님)
✅ ④ keep at it — 계속하다 ←정답
det.tip: keep at it = 계속하다, 꾸준히 하다 (포기하지 않고 지속)
